claim: Osteoporosis is a common systemic skeletal disorder resulting in bone fragility and increased fracture risk.
source: Osteoporosis is a common systemic skeletal disorder resulting in bone fragility and increased fracture risk.
evidence: This is a general statement about osteoporosis that draws from established scientific consensus.

claim: GAS5 was decreased in the bones and BMSCs of osteoporosis patients.
source: Our current research found that GAS5 was decreased in the bones and BMSCs, a major origin of osteoblast, of osteoporosis patients.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: GAS5 promotes osteoblast differentiation by interacting with UPF1 to degrade SMAD7 mRNA.
source: Mechanistically, GAS5 promotes the osteoblast differentiation by interacting with UPF1 to degrade SMAD7 mRNA.
evidence: This mechanistic claim is supported by multiple experimental approaches including RNA pull-down, RIP assays, and mRNA decay experiments shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Gas5 heterozygous mice showed decreased bone mass and impaired bone repair ability.
source: Moreover, a decreased bone mass and impaired bone repair ability were observed in Gas5 heterozygous mice, manifesting in osteoporosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT analysis, histological staining, and cranial defect experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Systemic supplement of Gas5-overexpressing adenoviruses significantly ameliorated bone loss in an osteoporosis mouse model.
source: The systemic supplement of Gas5-overexpressing adenoviruses significantly ameliorated bone loss in an osteoporosis mouse model.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo experiments using dexamethasone-induced osteoporosis mice treated with Gas5-overexpressing adenoviruses, shown in Figure 7.

claim: Over 200 million people worldwide suffer from osteoporosis.
source: Over 200 million people worldwide suffer from this disease, and this number is gradually increasing (Lizneva et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lizneva et al., 2018.

claim: Osteoporotic fractures cost $20 billion to $30 billion annually in the United States and European Union.
source: In the United States and European Union, osteoporotic fractures have been estimated to cost $20 billion to $30 billion annually (Lorentzon, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lorentzon, 2019.

claim: The imbalance between bone and fat mass is a typical feature of osteoporosis pathogenesis.
source: The imbalance between bone and fat mass is a typical feature of the osteoporosis pathogenesis (de Paula and Rosen, 2020; de Paula and Rosen, 2017; Infante and Rodríguez, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to de Paula and Rosen (2020, 2017) and Infante and Rodríguez (2018).

claim: Abnormal differentiation capacities of BMSCs play an important role in the pathogenesis of osteoporosis.
source: Recent studies have demonstrated that the abnormal differentiation capacities of bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) play an important role in this critical pathogenesis of osteoporosis (Li et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019 and Ma et al., 2018.

claim: BMSCs are stem cells that possess self-renewal and multiple differentiation abilities.
source: BMSCs are stem cells that possess self-renewal and multiple differentiation abilities (Grayson et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Grayson et al., 2015 and represents established knowledge about BMSCs.

claim: BMSCs are the major origins of osteoblasts and adipocytes.
source: As the major origins of osteoblasts and adipocytes, BMSCs maintain their balance between osteoblast and adipocyte, which are regulated by various molecular checkpoints (Anthony and Link, 2014; Williams and Hare, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Anthony and Link, 2014 and Williams and Hare, 2011.

claim: Long noncoding RNAs are a type of RNA longer than 200 nt and do not have protein-coding potential.
source: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are a type of RNA longer than 200 nt and do not have protein-coding potential (Marchese et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a definitional claim supported by a citation to Marchese et al., 2017 and represents established knowledge.

claim: LncRNAs are involved in BMSCs osteoblast and adipocyte differentiation.
source: Previous studies have revealed that lncRNAs are involved in BMSCs osteoblast and adipocyte differentiation (Xie et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xie et al., 2019.

claim: GAS5 negatively affected adipocyte differentiation through the miR-18a/CTGF pathway.
source: In our previous study, we demonstrated that GAS5 negatively affected the adipoytes differentiation through the miR-18a/CTGF pathway (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Li et al., 2018).

claim: Gas5 could promote osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells by FOXO1 in mouse.
source: For example, the researches of Wang, X etc. indicated that Gas5 could promotes osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells by FOXO1 in mouse (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2019.

claim: BGLAP and COL1A1 immunohistochemical staining confirmed the decrease in bone formation markers in osteoporosis patients.
source: BGLAP and COL1A1 immunohistochemical staining confirmed the decrease in the bone formation marker in osteoporosis patients (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical staining data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The mRNA level of GAS5 in both bone tissues and BMSCs was decreased in patients with osteoporosis compared to those with hip dysplasia and normal control.
source: The mRNA level of GAS5 in both bone tissues and BMSCs was decreased in patients with osteoporosis compared to in those with hip dysplasia and normal control (Figure 1B–C)
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: GAS5 was upregulated along with the induction of osteogenesis.
source: The results showed that GAS5 was upregulated along with the induction of osteogenesis, as shown by ARS assays, ALP staining, ALP tests and qPCR (Figure 1D–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple assays including ARS, ALP staining, ALP tests, and qPCR shown in Figure 1D-E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was a positive relationship between the expression of GAS5 and the quantification of ARS staining.
source: In addition, there was a positive relationship between the expression of GAS5 and the quantification of ARS staining (Figure 1F)
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: There was a positive relationship between the expression of GAS5 and ALP activity.
source: or ALP activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: There was a positive relationship between the expression of GAS5 and RUNX2/COL1A1/BGLAP mRNA expression.
source: or RUNX2/COL1A11/BGLAP mRNA expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–D) in osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B-D.

claim: The distribution of GAS5 was more abundant in the cytoplasm.
source: As shown in Figure 1G, the distribution of GAS5 was more abundant in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The cytoplasmic distribution of GAS5 remained unchanged after osteogenic induction.
source: This tendency remained unchanged after induction (Figure 1H–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by nuclear and cytoplasmic fractionation assays shown in Figure 1H-I.

claim: Decreased osteoblast differentiation was shown after decreasing GAS5 expression.
source: Decreased osteoblast differentiation was shown in the ARS assay (Figure 2B) and ALP assay (Figure 2C) after decreasing GAS5 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by ARS and ALP assay data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: The expression of osteogenesis markers (RUNX2, COL1A1, BGLAP, ALPL, and SP7) decreased after GAS5 knockdown at both mRNA and protein levels.
source: The expression of osteogenesis markers, including RUNX2, COL1A1, BGLAP, ALPL, and SP7, showed consistent results at both the mRNA (Figure 2D) and protein levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: New bone formation in the shGAS5 group was significantly lower than that in the control group in vivo.
source: The new bone formation shown by H and E, Masson staining and BGLAP immunohistochemical staining in the shGAS5 group was significantly lower than that in the control group (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo bone formation experiments with histological staining shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Osteoblast differentiation was significantly promoted after transfection with OE-GAS5.
source: After transfection with OE-GAS5, the osteoblast differentiation was significantly promoted, as determined by both ARS assays (Figure 3B) and ALP assays (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ARS and ALP assay data shown in Figure 3B-C.

claim: Increased bone formation in the OE-GAS5 group was observed in the bone formation model.
source: Moreover, increased bone formation in the OE-GAS5 group was observed in the bone formation model by H and E staining, Masson staining and BGLAP immunohistochemical staining (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo bone formation experiments with histological staining shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: No significant changes in the adjacent genes were observed after inhibiting GAS5 expression.
source: The results showed that no significant changes in the adjacent genes were observed after inhibiting GAS5 expression, indicating that it did not function through cis regulation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR analysis of adjacent genes shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: UPF1 was identified in the GAS5 pull-down assay by mass spectrometry.
source: The mass spectrometry results indicated that UPF1, a DNA/RNA helicase at the crossroads of many critical cellular pathways for RNA and DNA maintenance (Fiorini et al., 2018), was identified in the GAS5 pull-down assay (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data from RNA pull-down assay shown in Figure 4A, with additional context from citation to Fiorini et al., 2018.

claim: GAS5 could interact with UPF1 specifically.
source: Western blot analysis of the GAS5 pull-down protein confirmed that GAS5 could interact with UPF1 specifically (Figure 4B)
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot analysis of RNA pull-down shown in Figure 4B.

claim: RIP assay using the anti-UPF1 antibody confirmed the interaction between GAS5 and UPF1.
source: and a RIP assay using the anti-UPF1 antibody further confirmed this conclusion (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RIP assay data shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: The locations of GAS5 and UPF1 in BMSCs partly overlapped.
source: In addition, the locations of GAS5 and UPF1 in BMSCs partly overlapped, further indicating the interaction of GAS5 and UPF1 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: GAS5 (210–420) was indispensable in the interaction with UPF1.
source: RNA pull-down followed by western blot analyses showed that GAS5 (210–420) was indispensable in the interaction with UPF1 and GAS5 was unable to detect UPF1 when this sequence was lost (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA pull-down experiments with GAS5 truncation mutants shown in Figure 4G.

claim: UPF1-HD specifically combined with GAS5.
source: The results showed that UPF1-HD specifically combined with GAS5 (Figure 4I–J), which indicated that UPF-HD is indispensable in the interaction of GAS5 and UPF1.
evidence: This claim is supported by RIP assays with UPF1 truncation mutants shown in Figure 4I-J.

claim: The SMAD1/5/8 signaling pathway was significantly decreased in the shGAS5 group but increased in the GAS5-OE group.
source: As shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C, the SMAD1/5/8 signaling pathway was significantly decreased in the shGAS5 group but increased in the GAS5-OE group
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot analysis of pathway activation shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: The catenin and ERK pathways were impervious to GAS5 expression.
source: and the catenin and ERK pathways were impervious to GAS5 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: SMAD7 was increased in the GAS5 siRNA group and decreased in the GAS5 overexpression group.
source: Further exploration of the TGF-β/SMAD1/5/8 pathway revealed that SMAD7, an inhibitor of SMAD1/5/8 (Miyazawa and Miyazono, 2017), was increased in the GAS5 siRNA group and decreased in the GAS5 overexpression group (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B-C, with additional context from citation to Miyazawa and Miyazono, 2017.

claim: Other molecular factors in the SMAD1/5/8 pathways (BMP2, BMP4, BMP7 and SMAD6) were unchanged.
source: Other molecular factors in the SMAD1/5/8 pathways, such as BMP2, BMP4, BMP7 and SMAD6, were unchanged (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-F.

claim: UPF1 knockdown could increase the expression of SMAD7 and inhibit the activation of the SMAD1/5/8 pathway.
source: UPF1 knockdown could increase the expression of SMAD7 as well as inhibit the activation of the SMAD1/5/8 pathway (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: UPF1 could bind to SMAD7 mRNA.
source: First, we determined that UPF1 could bind to SMAD7 mRNA by a RIP assay (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RIP assay data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The SMAD7 mRNA decay speed was slower in the shGAS5 group but faster in the OE-GAS5 group.
source: Next, we tested the mRNA abundance after the addition of actinomycin D, which is an inhibitor of DNA transcription, and found that the SMAD7 mRNA decay speed was slower in the shGAS5 group but faster in the OE-GAS5 group at both the protein and RNA levels (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by actinomycin D chase experiments shown in Figure 5G-I.

claim: UPF1 knockdown completely blocked the effect of GAS5 on SMAD7 mRNA decay speed.
source: UPF1 knockdown completely blocked the effect of GAS5 on SMAD7 mRNA decay speed (Figure 5J).
evidence: This claim is supported by actinomycin D chase experiments with UPF1 knockdown shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The region of GAS5 (210–420 bp) could enhance the speed of SMAD7 mRNA decay and was blocked by UPF1 knockdown.
source: Furthermore, the region of GAS5 (210–420 bp) could also enhance the speed of SMAD7 mRNA decay and was blocked by UPF1 knockdown (Figure 5K).
evidence: This claim is supported by actinomycin D chase experiments with GAS5 truncation mutants shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Knocking down UPF1 expression blocked the function of GAS5 in the regulation of osteoblast differentiation.
source: Knocking down UPF1 expression obviously blocked the function of GAS5 in the regulation of osteoblast differentiation, as shown by ARS and ALP assays (Figure 5L–M).
evidence: This claim is supported by ARS and ALP assay data with UPF1 knockdown shown in Figure 5L-M.

claim: All homozygous Gas5-/- mice unexpectedly died during the embryonic period.
source: However, we used Gas5 heterozygotes (Gas5+/-) instead because all homozygous Gas5-/- mice unexpectedly died during the embryonic period.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the Gas5 knockout mouse model construction.

claim: Gas5 partly deletion was successful in Gas5+/- mice.
source: QRT-PCR analysis and DNA agarose gel electrophoresis proved that Gas5 partly deletion was successful (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR and gel electrophoresis data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Gas5 in cancellous bone of Gas5+/- mice decreased compared with the WT mice.
source: And Gas5 in cancellous bone of Gas5+/-mice decreased compared with the WT mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The heterozygous Gas5+/- mice survived normally and showed no changes in size, weight or appearance compared with their WT littermates.
source: The heterozygous Gas5+/- mice survived normally and showed no changes in size, weight or appearance compared with their WT littermates (Gas5+/+).
evidence: This claim is based on observational data from the Gas5+/- mouse model.

claim: The Gas5+/- mice had less femoral cancellous bone than the WT mice.
source: However, the Gas5+/- mice had less femoral cancellous bone than the WT mice, as shown by micro-CT and its three-dimensional reconstruction results (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Bone trabeculae were decreased in Gas5+/- mice.
source: In addition, H and E staining and Bglap immunohistochemical staining showed that bone trabeculae were decreased in Gas5+/- mice (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological staining shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: BV/TV, trabecular thickness, and trabecular number were decreased in Gas5+/- mice compared with WT mice.
source: In addition, bone analysis from micro-CT showed that BV/TV, trabecular thickness, and trabecular number were decreased, and BSA/BV and trabecular spacing were increased in Gas5+/- mice compared with in WT mice (Figure 6C–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT bone analysis shown in Figure 6C-G.

claim: BSA/BV and trabecular spacing were increased in Gas5+/- mice compared with WT mice.
source: In addition, bone analysis from micro-CT showed that BV/TV, trabecular thickness, and trabecular number were decreased, and BSA/BV and trabecular spacing were increased in Gas5+/- mice compared with in WT mice (Figure 6C–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT bone analysis shown in Figure 6C-G.

claim: Decreased Bglap levels in the sera of the Gas5+/- group were observed compared with those in the WT group.
source: As shown in Figure 6H, decreased Bglap levels in the sera of the Gas5+/- group were observed compared with those in the WT group.
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Gas5 was decreased in Gas5+/- mice while Smad7 was increased compared with WT mice.
source: Gas5 was decreased in Gas5+/- mice while Smad7 was increase compared with WT mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data from BMSCs of Gas5+/- and WT mice.

claim: The level of Upf1 mRNA has no significant change in Gas5+/- and WT mice.
source: However, the level of Upf1 mRNA has no significant change in two groups (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Gas5+/- mouse BMSCs manifested a decreased osteoblast differentiation ability.
source: ARS and ALP staining showed that Gas5+/- mouse BMSCs manifested a decreased osteoblast differentiation ability (Figure 6I–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by ARS and ALP staining data shown in Figure 6I-L.

claim: The Smad1/5/8 pathway was significantly lower in the Gas5+/- group.
source: Furthermore, the detection of proteins isolated from the tibia indicated that the Smad1/5/8 pathway, rather than the catenin and ERK signaling pathways, was significantly lower in the Gas5+/- group (Figure 6M–N, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot analysis of tibia proteins shown in Figure 6M-N and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: The bone repair area on cranial bone was lower in Gas5+/- mice than in WT mice.
source: Using micro-CT, we found that the bone repair area on cranial bone was lower in Gas5+/- mice than in WT mice (Figure 6O–P).
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT analysis of cranial defect repair shown in Figure 6O-P.

claim: The bone mass was alleviated after Gas5-overexpressing adenovirus injection as determined by micro-CT.
source: After Gas5-overexpressing adenovirus injection, the bone mass was alleviated as determined by micro-CT (Figure 7A)
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The bone mass was alleviated after Gas5-overexpressing adenovirus injection as shown by H and E staining and Bglap immunohistochemical staining.
source: as well as by H and E staining and Bglap immunohistochemical staining (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological staining shown in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: BV/TV, trabecular thickness and trabecular number were increasing in the Gas5 adenovirus group supplemented with drugs.
source: Bone analysis from micro-CT showed that the BV/TV, trabecular thickness and trabecular number were increasing in the Gas5 adenovirus group supplemented with drugs and had decreased BSA/BV and trabecular spacing compared with the negative control (Figure 7C–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT bone analysis shown in Figure 7C-G.

claim: BSA/BV and trabecular spacing decreased in the Gas5 adenovirus group compared with the negative control.
source: Bone analysis from micro-CT showed that the BV/TV, trabecular thickness and trabecular number were increasing in the Gas5 adenovirus group supplemented with drugs and had decreased BSA/BV and trabecular spacing compared with the negative control (Figure 7C–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT bone analysis shown in Figure 7C-G.

claim: GAS5 is a critical molecule in the osteoblast and adipocyte differentiation.
source: Considering all of these findings together, we concluded that GAS5 is a critical molecule in the osteoblast and adipocyte differentiation and contributes to the pathogenesis of osteoporosis
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the collective experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: GAS5 contributes to the pathogenesis of osteoporosis.
source: Considering all of these findings together, we concluded that GAS5 is a critical molecule in the osteoblast and adipocyte differentiation and contributes to the pathogenesis of osteoporosis
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the collective experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: BMSCs antagonistically perform osteoblast or lipoblast differentiation both in vivo and in vitro.
source: As the major originating cells of osteoblasts and adipocytes, BMSCs antagonistically perform osteoblast or lipoblast differentiation both in vivo and in vitro (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2018 and represents established knowledge.

claim: The lncRNA H19 could regulate osteogenesis by sponging miR-675 and associating with cartilage regeneration.
source: For example, the lncRNA H19 could regulate osteogenesis by sponging miR-675 and associating with cartilage regeneration, and abnormal H19 expression was found in patients with osteoarthritis (Huang et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2015 and Liu et al., 2017.

claim: Abnormal H19 expression was found in patients with osteoarthritis.
source: For example, the lncRNA H19 could regulate osteogenesis by sponging miR-675 and associating with cartilage regeneration, and abnormal H19 expression was found in patients with osteoarthritis (Huang et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2015 and Liu et al., 2017.

claim: SMAD7 inhibits the SMAD1/5/8 pathway and negatively regulates the osteoblast differentiation.
source: Studies have found that SMAD7 inhibits the SMAD1/5/8 pathway and negatively regulates the osteoblast differentiation (Li et al., 2017; Miyazawa and Miyazono, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2017 and Miyazawa and Miyazono, 2017.

claim: UPF1 is a key molecule in mRNA nonsense-mediated decay (NMD).
source: UPF1 is a key molecule in mRNA nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) (Dehecq et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dehecq et al., 2018 and represents established knowledge.

claim: UPF1 knockdown could inhibit the proliferation of colon cancer cells through the NMD mechanism.
source: Recent studies indicated that UPF1 knockdown could inhibit the proliferation of colon cancer cells through the NMD mechanism (Bokhari et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bokhari et al., 2018.

claim: The HD domain was the key functional area in UPF1-associated NMD.
source: The HD domain was the key functional area in UPF1-associated NMD.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about UPF1 structure and function.

claim: Mutations of the HD domain disrupt the RNA helicase activity of UPF1 and perturb the function of UPF1 in NMD.
source: Mutations of the HD domain disrupt the RNA helicase activity of UPF1 and perturb the function of UPF1 in NMD (Dehecq et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dehecq et al., 2018.

claim: The binding of GAS5 and UPF1 may strengthen the binding force of UPF1 and its target mRNA SMAD7.
source: Our results suggested that the binding of GAS5 and UPF1 may strengthen the binding force of UPF1 and its target mRNA SMAD7.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the experimental results.

claim: Decreased bone mass and increased fat formation in bone are the main histopathological manifestations of osteoporosis.
source: Decreased bone mass and increased fat formation in bone are the main histopathological manifestations of osteoporosis (Compston et al., 2019; Eastell et al., 2016; Infante and Rodríguez, 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Compston et al., 2019, Eastell et al., 2016, and Infante and Rodríguez, 2018.

claim: BMSCs in osteoporosis patients possess a decreased osteogenic ability but an enhanced adipogenic ability.
source: Many studies have confirmed that BMSCs in osteoporosis patients possess a decreased osteogenic ability but an enhanced adipogenic ability (de Paula and Rosen, 2020; Pagnotti et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to de Paula and Rosen, 2020 and Pagnotti et al., 2019.

claim: Global Gas5 knockout caused unexpected lethality in the embryonic period.
source: However, global Gas5 knockout caused unexpected lethality in the embryonic period, which indicated that Gas5 was indispensable in the development of the embryo.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the Gas5 knockout mouse model.

claim: Gas5 was indispensable in the development of the embryo.
source: However, global Gas5 knockout caused unexpected lethality in the embryonic period, which indicated that Gas5 was indispensable in the development of the embryo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Gas5-/- mice died during embryonic development.

claim: The osteoporotic phenotype was observed in surviving Gas5 heterozygous mice.
source: Interestingly, the osteoporotic phenotype, including lower bone mass, was macroscopically and microscopically observed in surviving Gas5 heterozygous mice, as shown by both micro-CT and histological staining, compared with in WT mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT and histological data from Gas5+/- mice.

claim: Decreased Gas5 levels may change heterozygote bone mass by regulating the osteoblast differentiation.
source: Combining the above results, we speculated that decreased Gas5 levels may change heterozygote bone mass by regulating the osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the experimental results.

claim: The bone repair ability of Gas5 heterozygous mice was significantly weakened.
source: To further confirm the abnormal osteogenic ability of Gas5 heterozygous mice, we constructed a cranial defect model and found that its bone repair ability was significantly weakened
evidence: This claim is supported by cranial defect repair experiments shown in Figure 6O-P.

claim: The mechanism of cranial bone formation may not be analogous to what is observed for bone formation and or bone healing in the long bone.
source: However, the mechanism of cranial bone formation may not be analogous to what is observed for bone formation and or bone healing in the long bone (Katsimbri, 2017; Catala et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Katsimbri, 2017 and Catala et al., 2019.

claim: The treatment of osteoporosis is currently mainly aimed at osteoclasts.
source: Currently, the treatment of osteoporosis is currently mainly aimed at osteoclasts (Ensrud and Crandall, 2017; Roux and Briot, 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ensrud and Crandall, 2017 and Roux and Briot, 2018.

claim: The new therapy with teriparatide has shown a more curative effect in osteoporosis.
source: and the new therapy with teriparatide has shown a more curative effect in osteoporosis (Minisola et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Minisola et al., 2019.

claim: Treatment options directed at osteoblasts are of great significance.
source: which suggests that treatment options directed at osteoblasts are of great significance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the success of teriparatide therapy.

claim: Adenoviruses containing lncRNAs were used to treat mice and showed a significant therapeutic effect in many diseases, including ischemic myocardial injury and cardiac regeneration.
source: Adenoviruses containing lncRNAs were used to treat mice and showed a significant therapeutic effect in many diseases, including ischemic myocardial injury (Cai et al., 2019) and cardiac regeneration (Ponnusamy et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cai et al., 2019 and Ponnusamy et al., 2019.

claim: The bone loss in the Gas5 overexpression group was more alleviated than the bone loss in the control group.
source: Micro-CT, H and E staining, and Bglap immunohistochemical staining showed that the bone loss in the Gas5 overexpression group was more alleviated than the bone loss in the control group.
evidence: This claim is supported by micro-CT and histological data from the osteoporosis treatment experiment shown in Figure 7.

claim: GAS5 acts as a protective target in osteoporosis by regulating osteoblast differentiation.
source: These findings consistently support the hypothesis that the lncRNA GAS5 acts as a protective target in osteoporosis by regulating osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the collective experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Gas5 not only participates in the pathogenesis of osteoporosis but also may be a promising therapeutic target.
source: These results indicate that Gas5 not only participates in the pathogenesis of osteoporosis but also may be a promising therapeutic target.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data, with speculation about therapeutic potential.

claim: More convincing evidence should be obtained by conducting experiments with an osteoblast-specific Gas5 conditional knockout mouse.
source: For example, more convincing evidence should be obtained by conducting experiments with an osteoblast-specific Gas5 conditional knockout mouse.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions and limitations of the current study.

claim: Eight osteoporosis patients who suffered from femoral neck fractures and eight patients with hip dysplasia and eight normal controls with car accident requiring surgery were recruited.
source: Eight osteoporosis patients who suffered from femoral neck fractures and eight patients with hip dysplasia and eight normal controls with car accident requiring surgery were recruited (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a description of the study design and patient recruitment.

claim: GAS5 expression was closely related to bone metabolism in osteoporosis.
source: The mRNA level of GAS5 in both bone tissues and BMSCs was decreased in patients with osteoporosis compared to in those with hip dysplasia and normal control (Figure 1B–C), which indicated that GAS5 expression was closely related to bone metabolism in osteoporosis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that GAS5 levels are decreased in osteoporosis patients.

claim: GAS5 positively regulated the osteoblast differentiation by interacting with UPF1 to accelerate SMAD7 mRNA decay.
source: These results indicated that GAS5 positively regulated the osteoblast differentiation by interacting with UPF1 to accelerate SMAD7 mRNA decay.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the mechanistic experiments presented in Figure 5.

claim: SMAD7 in the SMAD1/5/8 signaling pathway was the target of the GAS5/UPF1 complex.
source: These results determined that SMAD7 in the SMAD1/5/8 signaling pathway was the target of the GAS5/UPF1 complex.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental data showing GAS5 and UPF1 regulate SMAD7.

claim: GAS5 could affect SMAD7 mRNA stability by binding to UPF1 in BMSCs.
source: Based on the function of UPF1, a key molecule in mRNA nonsense-mediated decay, we hypothesized that GAS5 could affect SMAD7 mRNA stability by binding to UPF1 in BMSCs.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that was subsequently tested and supported by experimental data.

claim: In osteoblast differentiation, the increased expression of GAS5 combined with UPF1 strengthened the binding of UPF1 and SMAD7, leading to the accelerated degradation of SMAD7 and activation of the SMAD1/5/8 pathway.
source: We speculated that in osteoblast differentiation, the increased expression of GAS5 combined with UPF1 strengthened the binding of UPF1 and SMAD7, leading to the accelerated degradation of SMAD7 and activation of the SMAD1/5/8 pathway, ultimately promoting osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Gas5+/- mice exhibit an osteoporotic phenotype and impaired bone repair capacity.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that Gas5+/- mice exhibit an osteoporotic phenotype and impaired bone repair capacity.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the Gas5+/- mouse phenotyping data presented in Figure 6.

claim: Gas5 may be a promising therapeutic target in osteoporosis.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Gas5 may be a promising therapeutic target in osteoporosis.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the therapeutic efficacy data from Figure 7.

claim: GAS5 positively promotes the osteoblast differentiation in vitro and in vivo.
source: These results indicated that GAS5 positively promoted the osteoblast differentiation in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the GAS5 overexpression experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: GAS5 did not function through cis regulation.
source: The results showed that no significant changes in the adjacent genes were observed after inhibiting GAS5 expression, indicating that it did not function through cis regulation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that adjacent genes were not affected by GAS5 knockdown.

claim: UPF1 is a DNA/RNA helicase at the crossroads of many critical cellular pathways for RNA and DNA maintenance.
source: The mass spectrometry results indicated that UPF1, a DNA/RNA helicase at the crossroads of many critical cellular pathways for RNA and DNA maintenance (Fiorini et al., 2018), was identified in the GAS5 pull-down assay (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a description of UPF1 function supported by a citation to Fiorini et al., 2018.

claim: UPF-HD is indispensable in the interaction of GAS5 and UPF1.
source: The results showed that UPF1-HD specifically combined with GAS5 (Figure 4I–J), which indicated that UPF-HD is indispensable in the interaction of GAS5 and UPF1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RIP assay data with UPF1 truncation mutants.

claim: SMAD7 is an inhibitor of SMAD1/5/8.
source: Further exploration of the TGF-β/SMAD1/5/8 pathway revealed that SMAD7, an inhibitor of SMAD1/5/8 (Miyazawa and Miyazono, 2017), was increased in the GAS5 siRNA group and decreased in the GAS5 overexpression group (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SMAD7 function supported by a citation to Miyazawa and Miyazono, 2017.

claim: GAS5 was another critical checkpoint molecule for the osteoblasts and adipocytes differentiation by promoting osteogenesis and inhibiting adipogenesis.
source: Collectively, these in vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that GAS5 was another critical checkpoint molecule for the osteoblasts and adipocytes differentiation by promoting osteogenesis and inhibiting adipogenesis.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the current and previous findings about GAS5 function.
